extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory (readers of Mochizuki's IUT papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Formal definitions and structural conditions for 'species', 'specimens', 'mutations', 'mutation-histories', and 'observables' as used in the inter-universal Teichmüller theory; includes set-theoretic foundations (ZFC/ZFCG, Grothendieck universes) and illustrative examples. Intended as a precise language to formulate later constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck universe V axioms / V-set
rubrics_metrics.description: A (Grothendieck) universe V is a set satisfying: (i) V is transitive; (ii) N ∈ V; (iii) if x ∈ V then P(x) ∈ V; (iv) if x ∈ V then ⋃x ∈ V; (v) if x ∈ V, y ⊆ V, and f : x → y is a surjection then y ∈ V. A set E is a V-set if E ∈ V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These axioms are given verbatim and used to define universes and the notion of V-sets; they underpin the discussion of ZFC-models and V-relative absoluteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: ZFC-model and ZFCG-model / existence axiom (†G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with models (sets and ∈) of ZFC axioms, called ZFC-models. A ZFC-model that also satisfies the Grothendieck-school existence axiom (†G) — 'Given any set x, there exists a universe V such that x ∈ V' — is called a ZFCG-model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences of (†G) are recorded (e.g., given a set I and universes {Vi}i∈I there exists V with Vi ∈ V) and used to justify infinite ascending chains of universes V0 ∈ V1 ∈ V2 ∈ ...; remarks note subtle foundational issues and reference Feferman for justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence: closure under indexed collections of universes
rubrics_metrics.description: From (†G): Given a set I and a collection of universes Vi indexed by I, there exists a (larger) universe V such that Vi ∈ V for i ∈ I. In particular there exist infinite ascending chains of universes V0 ∈ V1 ∈ V2 ∈ ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used repeatedly to argue about inter-universal constructions; also contrasted with absence of infinite descending chains by the axiom of foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 0-species (S0) and 0-specimen
rubrics_metrics.description: A 0-species S0 is a collection of conditions given by a set-theoretic formula Φ0(E) involving an ordered collection E = (E1,...,En0) of sets (species-data). A 0-specimen of S0 is a specific ordered collection E in some ZFC-model that satisfies Φ0(E); write E ∈ S0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in any ZFC-model the 0-specimens of S0 form a set, S0 is called 0-small. The definition emphasizes that species are given by set-theoretic formulas (rules) rather than particular sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1-species (S1) acting on S0; 1-specimen
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1-species S1 acting on a 0-species S0 is given by set-theoretic formulas Φ1(E, E', F) and Φ1◦1(...) encoding: (a) when a collection F = (F1,...,Fn1) is a 1-specimen F : E → E' (domain/codomain are 0-specimens of S0); (b) how composites are recognized (Φ1◦1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, in some ZFC-model, E,E' ∈ S0 and F satisfies Φ1(E,E',F) then (E,E',F) ∈ S1. The presentation lists the exact form of the formulas and their roles in specifying morphisms (1-specimens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of composites for 1-specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two 1-specimens F : E → E' and F' : E' → E'' of S1 in some ZFC-model, there exists a unique composite F'◦F : E → E'' in that ZFC-model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This uniqueness is part of the definition (condition (c)) and ensures well-defined composition at the level of specimens; the text notes this is 'a priori' an abuse of notation when multiple composites could exist but the axioms require uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associativity of composition for 1-specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of 1-specimens F : E → E', F' : E' → E'', F'' : E'' → E''' of S1 in a ZFC-model is associative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly required (condition (d)); used to assert that species carry categorical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity 1-specimen id_E and identity laws
rubrics_metrics.description: For any 0-specimen E of S0 there exists a unique 1-specimen id_E : E → E (the identity 1-specimen) such that for any 1-specimens F' : E' → E, F'' : E → E'' one has F ◦ F' = F' and F'' ◦ F = F'' (identity laws).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supplies units for composition and is part of the categorical structure of S1 acting on S0.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1-smallness
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in any ZFC-model, for any two 0-specimens E,E' of S0 the 1-specimens F : E → E' form a set, then S1 is called 1-small (and S is 1-small accordingly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used later when asserting induced bijections on morphism-sets under mutation-equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species S = (S0,S1), specimens, and species-isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A species S is the pair (S0,S1). A 0-specimen = species-object; a 1-specimen = species-morphism. A species-isomorphism is a species-morphism F : E → E' admitting an inverse F' with composites equal to identity species-morphisms. A species-automorphism is an isomorphism with domain = codomain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One says S is i-small if Si is i-small. The emphasis is that species encode both objects and morphisms up to the given set-theoretic rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category determined by a species
rubrics_metrics.description: In a fixed ZFC-model, the category determined by S has as objects the species-objects of S in that model and as arrows the species-morphisms of S in that model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate verification; this is how species produce honest categories in models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-free i-specimen
rubrics_metrics.description: An i-specimen of S is model-free if it is equipped with a description via a set-theoretic formula that is 'independent of the ZFC-model in which it is given' — i.e., for any universes V1,V2 with V1 ∈ V2 the formula determines the same i-specimen relative to either universe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to single out specimens described absolutely across universe-extensions; important for 'inter-universal' considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutation M : S ⇢ S (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mutation M : S ⇢ S is a collection of set-theoretic formulas Ψ0, Ψ1 with: (a) Ψ0(E,E') mapping 0-specimens E to a uniquely determined E' = M(E); (b) Ψ1(E,E',F,F') mapping 1-specimens F : E → E' to a uniquely determined F' = M(F) with E'=M(E), E'(cid:11)=M(E(cid:11)), and compatibility with composites and identities. In a fixed ZFC-model, M determines a functor from the category determined by S to itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutations come with natural notions of composition and identity; they are functorial on specimens in each ZFC-model by construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of mutations (Z : M → M')
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of mutations Z : M → M' is a set-theoretic formula Ξ such that for each 0-specimen E there is a unique F = Z(E) : M(E) → M'(E) in S1, and these satisfy naturality: for any species-morphism F : E1 → E2 one has M'(F) ◦ Z(E1) = Z(E2) ◦ M(F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a fixed ZFC-model, Z gives a natural transformation between the functors determined by M and M'. If each Z(E) is a species-isomorphism, Z is an isomorphism of mutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutation-equivalence and mutation-quasi-inverse
rubrics_metrics.description: A mutation M is a mutation-equivalence if there exists a mutation M' and isomorphisms of mutations identifying M◦M' and M'◦M with identity mutations (i.e., M and M' are quasi-inverses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If S and S are 1-small, a mutation-equivalence induces bijections between species-morphism sets (and species-isomorphism sets) of corresponding objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutation-history H = ((Γ), S*, M*)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mutation-history H indexed by an oriented graph (Γ with branch orderings) consists of: (a) for each vertex v a species Sv; (b) for each oriented edge e from v1 to v2 a mutation Me : Sv1 ⇢ Sv2. The underlying graph may be assumed simply connected for simplicity in later constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutation-histories are species-theoretic analogues of diagrams of categories and underpin constructions of 'loops' and iterates; the ordering on branches is part of the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observable (S-valued) and core
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-valued covariant (resp. contravariant) observable V of a mutation-history H assigns to each vertex v an observation mutation Vv : Sv → S and to each edge e morphisms of mutations Ve : Vv1 → Vv2 ◦ Me (resp. Ve : Vv2 ◦ Me → Vv1). If all Ve are isomorphisms of mutations, V is a core; the property of being a core is called coricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core may be thought of as lying 'under' the entire mutation-history uniformly. Cores allow one to describe invariant (unaltered) parts of objects across mutations and to express altered portions via non-coric observables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of species as 'rules' / emphasis on formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: The essence of a species lies in the collection of rules (set-theoretic formulas) that govern construction of specimens, not in the specific sets that occur as species-objects or species-morphisms in particular ZFC-models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author likens species to 'programs' or 'deterministic algorithms' producing output data; warns about internal indeterminacy of programs (modifications that do not affect output) and urges attention to canonicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical guidance: do not always write formulas explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically the text will not write out set-theoretic formulas explicitly; instead one uses conventional descriptions of the mathematical objects involved, but must check that these are well-defined and do not depend on arbitrary choices not describable by set-theoretic formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This admonition is repeated: ensure independence from arbitrary choices and verify absoluteness conditions when adopting conventional descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-universal immunity: species unaffected by universe extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Because species-data are given by abstract set-theoretic formulas, the notion constituted by a species is immune to extensions of the universe (e.g., ascending chains V0 ∈ V1 ∈ V2 ...). 'Inter-universal geometry' allows relating geometries occurring in distinct universes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the rationale for the term 'inter-universal' and underlies later constructions that compare specimens across different universes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species examples: categories as species
rubrics_metrics.description: The notions of a (small) category and an isomorphism class of (covariant) functors between two given small categories yield an example of a species: 0-species ↔ 'category', 1-species ↔ 'isomorphism class of functors'. A 0-specimen ↔ particular small category; a 1-specimen ↔ particular isomorphism class of functors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One verifies species-isomorphisms correspond to equivalences of categories; this concrete example grounds the abstract definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species examples: topological spaces and universal coverings
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of a topological space and continuous map determines a species Stop. Universal coverings X~ → X of pathwise connected spaces and compatible maps between coverings (considered up to deck transformations) determine a species Su-top; species-morphisms of Su-top are given by such maps up to deck transformations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Left to the reader to write the exact set-theoretic formulas; these examples illustrate the scope of species to encode classical geometric constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of 'loops' via mutation-histories without violating foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Although ∈-loops (a ∈ b ∈ c ∈ ... ∈ a) cannot occur by the axiom of foundation, mutation-histories and species permit one to 'simulate ∈-loops' by considering species-objects at different ∈-levels and identifying them via mutations and mutation-histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motivates using category-like species (simpler species) because they make constructing such loops easier; motivates 'geometry of categories' and absolute anabelian geometry for reconstructing earlier-stage objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cores as invariants and description of altered parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Cores associated to a mutation-history are invariant under the mutations; one may apply cores to describe, by non-coric observables, the portions of objects that are altered by mutations in terms of the unaltered portions (cores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conceptual point of view 'plays a central role in the theory of the present series of papers' and is used repeatedly in later constructions.
